representative_questions.question: How does increasing the saturation temperature affect the average cell size of neat PMMA foams?
representative_questions.expected_answer: Increasing the saturation temperature leads to bigger cell sizes, with a range from 2 to 25 micrometers, due to a larger plasticization interval of the polymer-gas system.

representative_questions.question: How does the foaming temperature threshold for neat polystyrene (PS) compare to that of neat polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA)?
representative_questions.expected_answer: Foaming of PS is only possible at higher saturation temperatures (above 50-60 °C), whereas PMMA is capable of foaming across the entire temperature range studied (25-80 °C), including quasi solid state foaming at 25 °C.
representative_questions.why_kept: Only question of this type; no merge

representative_questions.question: What effect does the addition of the MAM block copolymer have on the CO2 absorption and resulting morphology of PMMA blends at low saturation temperatures?
representative_questions.expected_answer: The addition of MAM increases CO2 absorption (weight gain ratio) and enables the production of ultra-microcellular structures with an average cell size close to 0.1 micrometers at low saturation temperatures.

representative_questions.question: Why is the quantity of CO2 uptake (w1) considered an important thermodynamic parameter in the gas foaming process?
representative_questions.expected_answer: It quantifies the affinity of CO2 for the material and influences the final foam density and the plasticization of the polymer, which lowers the glass transition temperature (Tg) and allows more time for cell growth.

representative_questions.question: Why was supercritical CO2 (scCO2) selected as the medium for foaming these amorphous polymers?
representative_questions.expected_answer: Supercritical CO2 was selected because of its low critical conditions (31.1 °C and 73.8 bar), which provide advantageous properties such as tuneable solvent power, plasticization of glassy polymers, and higher diffusion rates.
